subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Reported speech with the past perfect; Activate Your English
outcomes: Report past statements using the past perfect
Talk about regrets with 'I wish' and 'If only'

tf.s: 'I forgot my keys,' he said. → He said he had forgotten his keys.
tf.why: The past simple moves back to the past perfect.

tf.s: In reported speech, the past simple often becomes the past perfect.
Verbs move back a tense because the reporting verb is in the present.
tf.why: They move back because the reporting verb is in the past.

tf.s: 'We didn't see him,' she said. → She said they had not seen him.
tf.why: Didn't see becomes had not seen.

tf.s: 'I wish I had studied more' is a regret about the past.
'If only I hadn't wasted my time' means the speaker is happy about wasting time.
tf.why: It means the speaker is sorry about it.

tf.s: 'I swam,' she said. → She said she had swam.
The past perfect of 'catch' is 'had caught'.
We can use 'If only' with a negative past perfect.
tf.why: For example, 'If only I hadn't wasted my time.'

tf.s: In reported speech, we never change the verb tense.
tf.why: After a past reporting verb, the tense usually moves back.

boxes.q: 'I lost my phone,' he said. → He said he ___ his phone.
'We bought a car,' they said. → They said they ___ a car.
'I didn't write it,' she said. → She said she ___ it.
boxes.why: Didn't write becomes had not written.

boxes.q: 'I took the bus,' Ali said. → Ali said he ___ the bus.

o: moving a verb back one tense
boxes.why: In reported speech, verbs move back a tense.

boxes.q: 'I found the key,' Sara said. → Sara said she ___ the key.
'I went home,' he said. → He said he ___ home.
In 'She told me she had forgotten', which is the reporting verb?
boxes.why: The reporting verb introduces the reported words.

mcq.q: Why do verbs move back a tense in reported speech?
o: Because the reporting verb is in the past
mcq.why: A past reporting verb like 'said' causes backshift.

mcq.q: Which sentence shows a regret about the past?
o: I wish I had studied more.

mcq.q: In reported speech, the past simple usually becomes the...
'I saw a film,' he said. Which report is correct?
o: He said he had seen a film.
He said he sees a film.
He said he has saw a film.
He said he will see a film.

mcq.q: 'We didn't eat lunch,' they said. Report it.
o: They said they had not eaten lunch.
They said they don't eat lunch.
They said they have not ate lunch.
They said they will not eat lunch.
mcq.why: Didn't eat becomes had not eaten.

mcq.q: Khalid missed the bus because he woke up late. Which regret fits?
o: If only I hadn't woken up late.
If only I don't wake up late.
If only I wake up late.
If only I won't wake up late.

mcq.q: Sara is sorry she didn't call her grandmother. What does she say?
o: I wish I had called my grandmother.
I wish I call my grandmother.
I wish I will call my grandmother.
I wish I calling my grandmother.
mcq.why: Wish + past perfect for a past regret.

mcq.q: What is the difference between 'I wish I started' and 'I wish I had started'?
o: 'Had started' is the correct past perfect for a past regret
mcq.why: Past regrets need the past perfect.

mcq.q: Why is 'He said he had forgotten his book' in the past perfect?
o: The forgetting happened before he spoke
mcq.why: The past perfect shows the earlier past action.

mcq.q: Which reported sentence contains a mistake?
o: She said she had swam in the sea.
She said she had swum in the sea.
He said he had caught a fish.
They said they had built a house.
